title: Introduce ambassador onboard bridge and compact release serializer
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: onboarding diverse model bundles from ecosystem partners often requires custom glue to translate external metadata and release artifacts into our canonical model registry format. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) an "ambassador" onboarding bridge that accepts partner bundles (compressed tar/zip with metadata.yaml, model weights, evaluation tokens), applies a lightweight normalization and validation pipeline, and emits a canonical onboarding manifest; and (2) a compact release serializer used by the registry to produce small changelog artifacts and delta bundles suitable for infra transfer, signing, and downstream consumption.

Design and scope: the ambassador bridge is implemented as a small service/cli that performs schema mapping (field remaps + optional heuristics for missing fields), provenance annotation (source, checksum, declared license), and a gentle compatibility fallback (attempts to map unknown tokenizer or architecture strings to closest known types). The compact serializer produces a deterministic, minimal changelog entry (profile diffs, numeric performance anchors, artifact fingerprints) and a signed manifest blob (for later verification during automated rollouts). This PR stops short of adding long-term storage hooks or signed kms integration — those follow-ups are tracked in ENG-4990.

What changed (high level): added an ambassador module under packages/ambassador-onboard, a serializer module under packages/release-serializer, adapters for three common partner bundle shapes (hf-snapshot, tarball-with-metadata, legacy-s3-layout), unit and integration tests that exercise round-trip onboarding and changelog generation, and CI workflows to lint and run fast integration tests. Also added docs/examples/ambassador-quickstart.md and a small migration helper script scripts/compactize-existing-changelogs.py.

Checklist: - [x] Schema mapping and validation logic - [x] Compact changelog format and serializer - [x] Adapters for hf-snapshot, tarball, legacy-s3 - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs + quickstart - [x] Linear tickets linked

Notes on compatibility and risk: the ambassador applies non-destructive transformations by default and annotates any inferred fields so downstream reviewers can audit choices. The serializer changes the shape of release artifacts that consumer tooling expects; to reduce risk we ship the serializer in parallel with the existing, verbose changelog writer and both are produced for two release cycles. Consumer migration is coordinated in PM-833.

Testing and CI: CI adds a new workflow (ci/ambassador-integration) which runs lightweight partner-bundle fixtures inside a containerized environment. On first run the integration suite flaked due to a race when calculating file checksums; fixed by adding deterministic file ordering in the serializer. Current CI status: all checks passing (unit, lint, integration).

Rollout plan: 1) Merge feature behind a feature flag registry.enable_ambassador_bridge = false 2) Run ambassador against a subset of internal partner bundles and compare produced manifests in the dev staging bucket 3) Flip the feature flag for onboarding-infra teams for one week to collect feedback 4) Deprecate verbose changelog after two successful cycles.

Related: ENG-4921 (onboard bridge design), PM-833 (partner onboarding roadmap), ENG-4990 (KMS signing follow-up).
